description.narrative:
Stakeholder Effects: Improved access to and quality of finance for MSMEs, including WOEs. The MSME finance gap in Uzbekistan, estimated before the COVID-19 outbreak, exceeded US$11.8 billion or approximately 18% of the countrys GDP. Given the extent of the pandemics impact, this gap is expected to have increased even further, making it critical to support the MSME segment. In addition, the Project may be supported with a Blended Finance component in the form of a Performance- Based Incentive to incentivize the Bank in achieving pre-agreed on lending targets to WOBs.
Resilience: IFC anticipates that the project will support resilience amongst microfinance and BOP finance providers by helping the market deal with the growing uncertainty and catalyzing investor response. Disrupted borrower cash-flows and increased risk perception for the segments has left banks reluctant to lend directly to MSMEs. Macroeconomic instability and uncertainty on the long-term viability of their operations has led to increased difficulties in accessing the funds needed to support the recovery and growth of their lending operations. By investing in DAVR, IFC will demonstrate to other investors the viability of supporting the sustainability and recovery of BOP FSPs.

The proposed investment to existing IFCs portfolio client, Private Joint Stock Commercial Bank DAVR-Bank (DAVR or the Bank) is a senior loan package of up to US$20 million equivalent comprising of : (i) a senior unsecured 3-year loan (incl. 1-year grace period) for the amount of up to US$10 million on IFCs own account (A Loan) or UZS equivalent, (ii) a senior unsecured 3-year loan (incl. 1-year grace period) for up to US$10 million or UZS equivalent, to be mobilized from institutional investors (B Loan), and (iii) a cross-currency swap for the notional amount disbursed in USD (the Project). The purpose of the project is to support the Bank to expand its presence in the micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) segment, including a carve out for gender financing of up to 40% of the loan proceeds to be on-lend to women-owned enterprises (WOEs).
